chapter: Philadelphia, New York and Sam Wooding in Europe
title: Wooding's show band and the first night in Berlin
summary: Wooding's band was an entertaining show band with singers, a comedian, Edith Wilson and chorus girls; opening in Berlin, waiters brought the band food in the dressing room.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: I see. And what was that band like?
Sam I thought had one of the greatest bands I'd ever heard. It was a very good band. We did mostly -- it was an entertaining band.
Had a lot of singing, glee clubs, you know, quartets, guys would sing in all kind of languages. Billy
Lewis, he sang in all kind of different languages. Bobby Martin and -- it was a show band.
We had Slow Kid Thompson as a comedian and Edith Wilson, and we had a few chorus girls, that went to Europe with Sam.
Well, we opened up at the Bauphant Palace [on Zoo.] A big theater there in Berlin.
Well, Sam, of course, already had an audience over there.
Oh, yeah, Sam -- Sam was the biggest egg I ever saw in Europe. I had never seen anybody as big as Sam.

Oh, man, we got there -- we got to Berlin there and we had [Greenley] and Drayton, famous dance team. And we right straight to the theater, we were late getting there and I'll never forget, we were in the dressing room, getting ready to go on the stage and I looked up -- out the window and saw all these waiters coming round the street, around the corner all carrying trays of food, and I didn't know what the heck was going on, they were bringing us food cause
we didn't have time to eat. And they were all coming in, all beautifully dressed and waiting on us, bringing us food at the dressing rooms to eat.
That must've been a very strange experience, coming from here with the situation the way it was here.
